title: Critical Review Panel Selection
description: One resolver-owned council roster, written once before any provider dispatch. The manifest exists so the dispatched panel is a durable digest-bound fact rather than a caller's recollection: the dispatcher consumes `selected` exactly and never adds, removes, reorders, or substitutes a member. Two fields go beyond the implementation packet's recommended shape on purpose. `packetPath`/`packetSha256` bind the packet bytes as well as the record bytes, closing the window in which a resolved packet is edited between resolution and dispatch; and `mode` accepts `qualification-canary`, the one narrow non-live resolution that lets a conditional critic earn its scoped cohort receipt without weakening live selection.

schemaVersion.description: Pins this manifest contract; a consumer that accepts an unknown version is guessing at what was dispatched.

panelId.description: The live panel definition this roster came from, so a manifest resolved under a superseded panel is visible rather than silent.

mode.description: Which resolution produced this manifest, not the record's review mode: `initial` is the full council for any record the gate answers `full-council` for (design, initial, or material-redesign), `targeted-refuter` is the separate single-claim falsification roster, and `qualification-canary` authorizes no live dispatch at all.

reviewRecordPath.description: Absolute path of the frozen record that authorized this roster; a relative path cannot identify one epoch across working directories.

reviewRecordSha256.description: Digest of those exact record bytes, so a record edited after resolution no longer matches the roster it produced.

subjectDigest.description: The record's proof-subject digest, joining this roster to the same frozen artifact and changed-file identity every receipt and reviewer result binds.

packetPath.description: Absolute path of the immutable packet whose record binding was verified; deliberate hardening beyond the packet's recommended shape.

packetSha256.description: Digest of those exact packet bytes, so a packet mutated between resolution and dispatch is detectable rather than assumed unchanged.

selected.description: Every reviewer this resolution authorizes, in resolver order. An empty roster is never a valid dispatch.

skipped.description: Every conditional critic that was considered and not selected, with all of its reasons. Skipped is not missing: it never becomes a failed member and never blocks the unconditional council.

then.description: A full council always contains at least one unconditional critic, so a conditional skip can never shrink the panel to the conditional lane alone.
Targeted refutation is a distinct fixed roster: no conditional critic is ever selected or considered for it.
A qualification canary names exactly one conditional candidate and no unconditional reviewer, so it is structurally unusable as a council roster and cannot be mistaken for live authorization.

reasonCode.description: Closed on purpose. A selection or skip reason nobody declared is not auditable, so a new reason costs a schema change -- which is the moment anyone decides whether it is a real routing fact.

family.description: The reviewer family as named by the live panel definition; the join key for its result, receipt, and ledger rows.

agent.description: The exact agent definition to dispatch, so the roster cannot be satisfied by a similarly named reviewer.

lens.description: The configured primary lens. Independent lenses are what make several results evidence rather than repeated votes.

model.description: The exact provider/model[:effort] selector, including effort: a served model that differs from this is a mismatch, never an acceptable substitution.

evidence_delivery.description: Whether this member verifies claims through its own read-only repository tools or only from evidence pasted into its assignment.

selectionClass.description: `unconditional` members run on every full council; a `conditional` member is additive and never replaces or falls back to another family.

reasonCodes.description: Why this member is on the roster, recorded so selection is reconstructable from the manifest alone.

then.description: A conditional member is selected by a named eligibility policy or by the qualification-canary path, never by a configured-roster reason.

family.description: The conditional critic that was considered and not selected.

selectionClass.description: Only a conditional critic can be skipped; an unconditional critic that is absent is a resolution failure, not a skip.

reasonCodes.description: Every independent reason the packet was ineligible, sorted. All of them are recorded because a packet ineligible on three grounds is a different fact from one ineligible on a single ground.
